mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 700K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 700K units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, driving down discount rates and yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, always.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) drops below 8% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) shows a 3-month average increase of over 200K, the combined labor market strength predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both labor market conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeding 2% YoY, indicating a strong supply side, positively influences S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: During tightening cycles, walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increasing by more than 5% YoY, signaling robust demand, leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, always.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between RSAFS and stock market performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 55% of instances when RSAFS YoY growth exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 50 basis points within a quarter, indicating a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances following such a FEDFUNDS decrease.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 7% and the payroll employment (PAYEMS) to population ratio increases by more than 1% over 6 months, the labor market's dual strength predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only in early-cycle expansions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 7% and PAYEMS/pop ratio increase > 1% in 6mo
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market and stock market correlations
failure_condition: During early-cycle expansions, SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 45% of instances when both labor conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: GDP (GDPC1) growth rate exceeding 3% YoY, indicating strong aggregate demand, always predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of the regime.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.04 over any 2.5-year rolling window.
